blocking.finding: New in round 3. The documented abort would not stop the trial, and would damage its record. The runner header (lines 18-19) and HOST_NOTE:37 both say 'To abort: stop the launcher, scripts/run_bounded.py; the runner then records the end as usual.' run_bounded.py has no signal handler. It starts run_local_episode.py in a new session (start_new_session=True) and signals that session only on its own deadline. Stopping run_bounded.py therefore ends only the supervisor. It writes no process.json, while run_local_episode.py, the worker and the podman clients keep running. The runner's 'wait' then returns and 'finish normal' runs. That step stops the sampler, finds the main container still running, tars and stops it, and removes it under a live worker. It then hashes a run directory that the orphaned launcher and worker go on writing, until the worker hits its own wall or physics limit. This matters only if an abort is needed, but then it would leave the single trial's record inconsistent.
blocking.evidence: 2026-09-26_newton_macos_policy/scripts/run_bounded.py:45-57 (start_new_session=True; os.killpg only on its deadline; no handler); scripts/run_local_episode.py:269-271 (container client and worker in the launcher's process group); v33_trial_run.sh:18-20,74-89,142-145; versions/v33/HOST_NOTE_gpu5070ti.md:37
blocking.suggestion: Abort by signalling the launcher's process group, as run_bounded's own deadline does: kill -TERM -- -<pid of scripts/run_local_episode.py>, which leads its session. run_bounded then records the exit in process.json and the runner finishes normally. Alternatively, make the runner's TERM trap forward TERM to that process group and then take the normal path. Correct the header and the note to match.

non_blocking.finding: Wording only. The runner traps only SIGTERM in practice. Started as 'setsid nohup bash ... &' from a non-interactive shell, the runner starts with SIGHUP ignored (by nohup) and SIGINT and SIGQUIT ignored (as an asynchronous command). Bash cannot trap or reset signals that were ignored on entry, so 'trap ... INT HUP' has no effect. The sampler, run_bounded, the launcher, the worker and the podman clients inherit these ignored signals. No component relies on INT or HUP, and native_graph.py installs its own handlers, so nothing changes in function.
non_blocking.evidence: v33_trial_run.sh:7,66,103; bash manual: signals ignored on entry to a non-interactive shell cannot be trapped or reset; scripts/native_graph.py:33-34
non_blocking.suggestion: Write 'SIGTERM' in the runner header and in HOST_NOTE:38-40.

non_blocking.finding: After a SIGTERM to the runner alone, the manifest describes a run still in progress. The launcher keeps writing into runs/<ID>, and run_bounded later appends its final record to the runner log, which is its stdout. The manifest therefore cannot verify the final copy, the host record ends at the signal, and no post-run cleanup follows. A smaller edge case: a TERM that arrives during the 3-5 s snapshot block runs the trap while stdout is still redirected to _prerun.txt, so the 'finishing' lines land there instead of in the runner log. HOST_NOTE:38-40 says the manifest covers 'what exists', which is true only at that instant.
non_blocking.suggestion: State that after a runner-only kill the launcher group must also be ended (as in B7), and that the manifest is then recomputed once it has stopped. Alternatively, forward TERM to the launcher group in the trap, which also removes this case.

non_blocking.finding: The uid check, not redaction, is what protects other users. The check holds in the new dry runs: none of 29 other-user sampler entries and none of 610 other-user snapshot rows carry a command line. The only theoretical bypass is pid reuse between reading /proc/<pid> ownership and reading its cmdline, which is impractical with pid_max 4,194,304. For the invoking user's own processes, redaction is best effort. In synthetic tests it caught keyword flags, their '=' form and long mixed-case runs. It missed flags without a keyword (-p), URL user:password@ credentials, values quoted inside 'bash -c' strings (the value class excludes quotes), and tokens shorter than 32 characters or split by '/'. The snapshot's top section shows names only because this host has no toprc. A saved toprc with command-line display would print every user's command line.
non_blocking.evidence: host_sampler_linux.py:38-43,60,109-117,132; checks_out/runner_dry2/*_host.jsonl and *_prerun.txt (counts only); no ~/.toprc or ~/.config/procps/toprc on gpu5070ti; /proc mounted without hidepid
non_blocking.suggestion: Optional hardening: open /proc/<pid>/cmdline, then compare fstat(fd).st_uid with the uid. Add patterns for '://user:pass@' and quoted values. Run top with an empty HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME. Also state these limits in the note.
